1girl, solo, moon, full moon, curtain, kneeling, from above, foreshortening, reaching, looking at viewer, closed mouth, calm expression

An enormous flat ivory-white full moon is tilted in space like a round sheet of luminous paper, not a landscape. Character 1 kneels sideways along its lower curved rim, one knee supporting her weight and the other leg folded under her robe. She is caught halfway through peeling a heavy sheet of night away from the lunar disc. One hand braces on the curved ivory rim behind her shoulder. Her other arm reaches down and toward the camera, gripping the edge of a broad charcoal-teal curtain. The dark curtain is pulled diagonally into the lower-right foreground, uncovering the large uninterrupted pale circular face of the moon behind her. Her torso twists naturally between the bracing hand and the pulling arm. Her head turns back toward the viewer, both golden eyes readable, mouth neutral and brows relaxed. The camera is above and in front of her at a steep oblique angle, close enough that the pulling hand and curtain are enlarged in the foreground. Her face lies in the upper-left third, the near hand in the lower-right third, and the moon fills most of the upper-right field. The pale braid and white skirt sweep in an opposing arc along the moon rim, revealing the support of the knee and continuity of her body. The dark cloth folds are a few sweeping heavy shapes with a clearly pinched edge in her fingers, not smoke or tentacles. Leave broad quiet space within the moon; its circular outline remains legible and partly extends beyond the upper edge. Surround the disc with subdued charcoal-green and gray-violet abstract color planes. The pale moon supplies soft reflected light to her face and sleeve. Use the muted teal cape, pale hair, ivory moon and one small warm-gold eye accent as the limited color hierarchy. The action reveals completeness and new power through uncovering the full moon, not through an energy beam or an explosion. One coherent scene, no stars or floating ornaments used to fill empty space.

masterpiece, best quality, painterly, sketch, visible brush strokes, loose hand-painted texture, broken edges, blocky volume modeling.

A complete illustration with the freshness of a painted sketch, not an unfinished draft. Soft directional light reveals the planes of forms. Build volumes from confident planes of light and shadow with visible brush edges, while letting selected outer contours remain open. Use broad flowing paint masses, dry uneven strokes, and crisp small highlights appropriate to each material. Vary the brush size and edge sharpness between different materials. Preserve deliberate brush marks instead of smoothing every surface.
